newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bkk Bank Commerce revises up 1996 losses.
newsitem.headline: Bkk Bank Commerce revises up 1996 losses.

text.p: Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc said on Friday it had revised net losses for 1996 to a hefty 24.85 billion baht ($955.8 million) after the central bank instructed it to raise provisions for doubtful and non-performing loans.
The 1996 results were revised from a previously announced unaudited 1996 net loss of 2.84 billion baht.

Financial statements filed by the bank to the Thai stock exchange said the bank's 1996 net loss, up from a 860.4 million baht profit in 1995, could be attributed to its 27.2 billion baht provisions for doubtful loans against 3.2 billion a year ago.

The bank, which the government took over last May after the size of its non-performing loans was revealed in parliament, told the bourse its net non-performing loans, after collateral deduction, rose to 53.78 billion baht at end-1996 from 36.58 billion a year ago.
It said the Bank of Thailand asked the bank to set aside at least an additional 22 billion baht provisions for delinquent loans last year.
The bank also used another two billion baht of its retained earnings to cover the sharply higher doubtful loans which, it said, had mostly been extended during 1994 and 1995.
